about: Expected port-suite failures on the one compiler. Each entry names the failing tests, why they fail, and the plan task that owns them (docs/migration/index.md). The port runner (scripts/ports.mjs) diffs failing-test sets against this ledger: a failure not listed here is a regression, and a listed failure that passes must be removed. Test names are exactly as the runner parses them; names in parentheses are the runner's pseudo-failures (docs/testing.md). Recorded from the pre-M1 fleet run of 2026-09-23 (binary ~/lilscript-work/bin/pre-m1/lilscript, 26 ports, 21 fully green) and re-checked with scripts/ports.mjs on 2026-09-24: the node:test spec reporter reports a failing test and its failing parent suite as two names; monacolil's check:site passes, so its entry was removed; On 2026-09-24, after the M2.8/M2.9 release committed each goal port's rewrite to its repository, mdast-util-from-markdownlil, remark-parselil and react-markdownlil ran green with `--patches none` (binary release-m1) and their entries were removed. On 2026-09-27 (batch A1) mobxlil's build and suite, and the site-receipt tests of mdast-util-from-markdownlil and remark-parselil, were ledgered: they fail identically on head-070a7d4c. mobxlil's three upstream-path entries stay: its suite ran no test on either binary, so the runner's report that they pass was an artifact, which `suiteRan` now prevents.

entries.owner: M2.8 (fix the port's upstream-test path mapping when its rewrite is committed)

entries.reason: Its lilscript.toml sets `javascript.priority = "realistic-performance-first"`, which the compiler refuses (size is the objective; M3's honest configuration), so the build fails and jest runs against no fresh dist. With the key removed in a scratch copy the build completes, and every jest suite still fails to load: the development bundle calls `objectConstructor()`, a host global `src/host.lil` declares `extern` and the test environment does not define. Identical on head-070a7d4c and on batch A1's binary.
entries.owner: M12.2 (the port's rebuild on the current compiler: drop the refused key, define its host globals for the development bundle)

entries.reason: Upstream's test runs recheck's static ReDoS analysis over every zod regex under a fixed 60 s timeout. On this 8-core host at load 13-18 it takes 80-86 s and times out, on every binary; unloaded it passes (the 2026-09-24 release ran 1353/1353). It checks upstream's regex sources, not the compiler's output.
